title: Acids, Bases, and Salts - Chemistry - Salt Hydrolysis
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Predict the nature of an aqueous solution of sodium chloride ($NaCl$).
questions.explain: $NaCl$ is formed from a strong acid ($HCl$) and a strong base ($NaOH$), so it does not hydrolyze. The solution is neutral.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: An aqueous solution of ammonium chloride ($NH_4Cl$) will be:
questions.explain: $NH_4Cl$ comes from a weak base ($NH_3$) and a strong acid ($HCl$). The cation $NH_4^+$ hydrolyzes to produce $H^+$, making the solution acidic.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which salt will form a basic solution when dissolved in water?
questions.explain: $K_2CO_3$ is derived from a strong base ($KOH$) and a weak acid ($H_2CO_3$). The carbonate ion ($CO_3^{2-}$) hydrolyzes to form $OH^-$, making the solution basic.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why do solutions of small, highly charged metal cations like $Al^{3+}$ react as acids?
options: They hydrate and the hydration complex releases protons.
They react with $H^+$ to form precipitates.
questions.explain: Metal cations like $Al^{3+}$ form hydrated complexes (e.g., $[Al(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$) which then donate a proton to water, acting as weak acids.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: For a salt derived from a weak acid and a weak base, how do you determine if the solution is acidic or basic?
options: Compare the $K_a$ of the cation and $K_b$ of the anion.
questions.explain: If $K_a$ (cation) > $K_b$ (anion), the solution is acidic. If $K_b$ > $K_a$, it is basic. If equal, it is neutral.
questions.subject: Chemistry
